summary: Monolith: Django + Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL serving Django templates + HTMX, hosted on Google Cloud Run (us-central1 Iowa). Estimated $25-110/month (around the $100 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: A single deployable is the fastest and cheapest option for a 1-person team building a web_app with 5,000 users. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 1 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - Server-rendered templates + HTMX: Chosen because team already works in python (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; form-heavy CRUD screens render well on the server; gentle learning curve suits a beginner team on a 10-week timeline.

alternatives.why_not: No javascript/typescript in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk (fit 3.0 vs 7.4).
No javascript/typescript in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. Server-rendered templates + HTMX scores higher on cost and operational simplicity (fit 2.5 vs 7.4).

tradeoffs: Rich offline/canvas-style interactivity still needs JavaScript islands
UI and backend deploy together (fine for one team)

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in python (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3.

alternatives.why_not: Django scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 8.2 vs 8.9).
No csharp/fsharp in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. Django scores higher on platform coverage and time-to-market (fit 4.5 vs 8.9).

database.choice: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (us-central1 Iowa, HA standby)
database.justification: Chosen because strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=3. Managed as Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: same platform and private network as the application hosting; fully managed: no operations work for a team without DevOps.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 4.0 vs 4.7).
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 3.6 vs 4.7).
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on integration with the hosting platform (fit 0.3 vs 3.1).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud: self-managed VMs/databases are excluded in favour of managed services.

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale

hosting.justification: Chosen because multi-zone redundancy for availability 99.99%; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3.

alternatives.why_not: Google Cloud Run scores higher on learning curve and operational simplicity (fit 6.2 vs 7.2).
Google Cloud Run scores higher on cost and scalability (fit 5.7 vs 7.2).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud is not on-premise.

tradeoffs: Session affinity is best-effort for stateful rooms

supporting.justification: Chosen because auth inside the backend; no per-MAU fees; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=3.

alternatives.why_not: Django auth + django-allauth scores higher on authentication fit and cost (fit 2.8 vs 3.6).
Weaker cost efficiency (2/5) with priorities.cost=3. Django auth + django-allauth scores higher on authentication fit (fit 2.6 vs 3.6).

tradeoffs: You own password storage, rate limiting and MFA flows

supporting.justification: Chosen because free minutes, large action marketplace, works with any cloud; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3.

alternatives.why_not: Different cloud from the application hosting. GitHub Actions scores higher on time-to-market and cost (fit 1.1 vs 4.6).
Self-hosting CI is unnecessary; needs ongoing operations work but team.has_devops=false (ops burden 3/5). GitHub Actions scores higher on time-to-market (fit 0.3 vs 4.6).

supporting.justification: Chosen because same cloud/platform and region as the application; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3.

alternatives.why_not: Google Cloud Logging + Monitoring scores higher on integration with the hosting platform and scalability (fit 3.6 vs 6.0).
Different cloud from the application hosting (fit 1.5 vs 6.0).

supporting.justification: Chosen because strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=3.

alternatives.why_not: Different cloud from the application hosting. Resend scores higher on time-to-market (fit 1.5 vs 2.8).
In-network SMTP relay. Resend scores higher on maintainability and performance (fit -0.6 vs 2.8).

assumptions: Order-of-magnitude band from approximate public list prices (USD) in the knowledge base; not a quote
Sized for 5,000 users at 12 months, 100 peak concurrent users, ~15 req/s peak (scale tier: tiny)
Data: ~10 GB in the database, ~0 GB of media, ~73 GB/month egress
Excludes taxes, developer salaries, domain names, app-store fees and one-off migration work

breakdown.basis: tiny tier (~15 req/s peak, 100 concurrent users); x2.2 for redundant instances (availability 99.99%)
tiny tier instance; x3.0 for standby/replicas (availability 99.99%)

warnings.message: availability=99.99 (~4.3 min downtime/month) needs multi-region failover and 24x7 on-call; a 1-person beginner team without DevOps cannot operate that.
99.99% needs active-active or warm-standby in a second region; the stack is multi-zone in one region (~99.95%) plus cross-region replicas. Budget for the second region.
Expected $25-110/month: the upper end exceeds the $100 budget at peak usage. Set billing alerts.

assumptions: No data_residency or user geography given; primary region defaults to US East (move it next to your users)
RELAXED requirements.availability: designed for ~99.95% on managed multi-zone services (provider SLAs) instead of self-operated 99.99% multi-region failover
